overall: The AG found the Fall River School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by holding Feb 22 and Mar 8 meetings that were not accessible to the public, but found no intentional violation and no coordinated police exclusion.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee limited room access to its Feb 22 and Mar 8 meetings, letting them in late or only for public comment, and then asking them to leave.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by denying access to its February 22 and March 8 meetings when it did not allow members of the public into the meeting room for the duration of those meetings.

allegations.summary: The meeting notices listed only a physical room and did not say the public could attend remotely, though the committee relied on cable and Facebook broadcasts as alternative access.
allegations.key_passage: Although we understand that it may be the Committee’s regular practice to broadcast its meetings live on cable television and Facebook, meeting notices must include the location at which the public may access the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the committee's denial of access was intentional, which would make the violation a knowing one.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee did not intentionally violate the law when it failed to provide access to its meetings on February 22 and March 8.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged police and the committee coordinated a heavy police presence to keep the public out of the Feb 22 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: we find that the Committee did not seek the support of law enforcement for the purpose of excluding the public from its meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
